FluxMongers

This is a tiny companion collection to MAGNETIK which also celebrates my 6 full months (January 3rd, 2022 to July 3rd, 2022) in generative art, Yaaay! :) I imagined the FluxMongers to be the cause of the tear and distortion in MAGNETIK. 

I would like to thank everyone very much for the support and love you have shown me in these 6 months and hope you enjoy this small gift from me. Cheers!

A little info about the work itself:

- 12 palettes,
- 2 types of handedness : left and right,
- Their favorite number is the amount of ellipses the algo uses to draw their image :)
- A few hidden traits that may or may not appear :)

After going live,

- press ‘1’ to get a hi-res version and ‘2’ to get a medium-res version (hopefully it will work :/)

- press 's' to save a png
15760.c:
FluxMongers are very old beings from another dimension and their spin produces huge amounts of energy and this energy discharge is what causes the realities of MAGNETIK to be distorted or even to be torn apart. Their ethereal nature, speed and might make their movements almost to be perceived as some kind of choreography but this can only be called a dance of destruction. What you are looking at is a frame frozen in their deadly dance…

FluxMongers were inspired by light paintings where the painter uses one or few sources of light to draw in the air very quickly and the drawing is captured by long exposure.

What happens when your brain overloads, or when you lose control of your giant robot.

A study on the repetition and stacking of a simple but very dynamic structure.

Everything procedurally generated at runtime.
You can find more informations on the piece, its design and origins, here: https://ulucode.com/wp/neural-collapse/

Interactivity : 
- You can hover your mouse on the connectors to close them... temporarily
- Press and hold the mouse button to slightly move the viewpoint.

- Press "a" to increase quality of the antialiasing (3 levels), at the cost of performances. Especially useful on the palettes using outlines.
- Export a PNG capture at various resolutions by pressing the number keys 1 to 9 (top row or numpad, and only in live mode, after pressing "open"). Resolutions ranges from 720 to 7680 pixels. I recommend starting with "4".

GPU recommended. Best performances on Chrome in general.

15787.d:
"The Department of Military Experimental Biotechnology on planet Uctumi has announced that spiders designed to combat the Alienpillars plague are ready for deployment. The Impure Spiders are genetically modified and nanotechnology-enhanced arachnids and are expected to be the final solution to this serious crisis after the failure of pesticides."

The sequel to Alienpillars. For this work I used a mixed technique with shaders and line drawing in p5.js A first pass sets the main raymarching shader in data output mode, and encodes the surface data which is then used in p5.js to draw the lines in realtime. This hair layer is then combined with a second pass in normal shading mode. Another post-processing pass applies the bloom effect and draws the frame.

Everything is generated by code. Drag mouse to rotate the camera.


Notes: 

- It is CPU and GPU intensive. It can run slow on low end machines and is not meant to be run on mobile devices. 
- Part of this project uses modified code from "Verlet Spider!" shader at Shadertoy website. Thanks to Dave Hoskins for allowing me to use it.
- I would like to thank the guys at GNFTS Discord server for all the support during the coding sessions on the cowork voice channel.


Features:

- Spider color and patterns
- Eye position and color
- Head and ass sizes
- Length and thickness of legs
- Final camera height

Special editions:

- Glitch (20%)
- Sketch (10%)
- Neon (5%)

15826.d:
A Generative Art Project by Matthew Hawtin & Murat Atimtay. Smooth-brained is part of the fxhash live minting experience at Proof of People, London 2022.

The initial visual idea for ‘Smooth-brained’ was to use one pixel and a two-colour gradient in multiple ways across a grid, using repetition, orientation, placement and scale, resulting in a visual composition that became the genesis piece. From that original artwork, Murat took the premise and through creative-coding, began to expand and experiment on the parameters, introducing new visual possibilities and paving the way for this collaborative generative art collection. The beauty of a gradient is that it gives the impression of depth and form on a 2D surface. This allows the visual fields to seem outward and also inward while giving the impression of movement within the whole piece and within individual cells; conjuring up spaces within spaces. The compositions are meant to be spaces for the eye to roam, decorative yet functional, complex yet minimal, a place where the brain is pleased and not duly complicated - a state of ‘smooth-brained’.

Press 1 to 8 export PNG between 1000px to 8000px

15857.d:
While experimenting with some Victor Vasarely's graphics, my work kept making me think about people taking refuge in the steel mills in Ukraine. Looking at the iterations, it seemed to me that I was looking outside the shelter, not fully understanding what was happening on the other side of the grate. The fate of those people in Ukraine is also very similar to that of my hometown during the Second World War, because we have a large steel mill here too.
Since I couldn't get rid of it, despite all the tests I did, I decided to stick with that idea.
For the typography variation, I took inspiration from Alighiero Boetti's work.
A huge thank you to Valentina Taddei who helped me focus on what was important.

15880.d:
This project is a study and exploration in the fields of Abstract Expressionism and Algorithmic Art. I am trying to find a middle way between a humanistic expressive look and feel, and a computational structural foundation underneath it. First I shape and sculpt a simplex noise field to have a base structure to work with. Second I slice it up in layers where some layers are removed and others are being kept as the final sculpture. Third I draw strokes of the remaining layers and give it an expressive style. 

I have no designs for the brush strokes, it is all generated as a consequence of how the system is programmed on what to reveal and what not to reveal. There are strict ranges where the noise field stays in which give certain consistent visuals, but they are random ranges and not fixed designs. This decision gave a lot of room for interesting random strokes, as if the algo is brushing expressively.  

I have only scratched the surface of sculpting noise fields and drawing an image out of it. To think about the possibilities of algorithmically shaping structures and drawing an expressive artpiece is just mind-boggling. The project title is hinting on the potential of these artpieces, where inspiration to further develop this art domain is hiding in plain sight.

Hotkey
s - to save an image as PNG - 8000 x 5000

BLOCKSTARS is a cross platform project on fxhash and 8bidou pointing out the importance of longevity of NFT art. The project consists of 100 hand drawn 24x24 px avatars.

This is my first conceptional artwork showing the difference between off and on-chain nfts.

The collector generates an off-chain token on Fxhash pointing to the on-chain artwork stored on 8bidou. The Fxhash token servers as a link to the original artwork pointing to the stored image.

The QR code is the reference to off-chain images data storage on the blockchain that is revealed via the image scan linking to the visible on-chain artwork.

In on-chain the token itself is the artwork which is stored directly on the blockchain.

After the reveal of the QR code the unique 1/1 24x24 pixel Blockstar will be airdropped to the first collector. The art and the metadata is stored within the token itself, making it as immutable as the blockchain itself.

ART + METADATA = NFT

The projects aims to show the importance of decentralized data security in web3. to guarantee the longlivity of the artwork it’s using the on-chain technology limited for now available for artists on the tezos blockchain.

* made with love on p5

* press "s" to save image

Polar Grid is part of the fxhash live minting experience at Proof of People, London 2022.

This is a study of color, motion, and composition, and an homage to cinema as an artform. Colorful shapes overlap and pulse in a ever repeating dance. An abstracted movie experience. Each color palette in the series (except one) is inspired by a different film director (if you want a real challenge, see how many you can guess without looking at the feature names).

The palettes were extracted from movie stills or movie posters and fine tuned by hand. As often, I have to thank independent tool makers for their indirect help. My gratitude goes to David Aerne for FarbVélo and Fabrizio Bianchi for Coolors.

The code for Polar Grid is based on early iterations of what ultimately became my carat series. Both projects come from the same fascination for color as a system, even though I used a different approach here. You could call this a carat prequel.

The animation is done using a technique called polar noise. This makes it so the motion of all elements ends up repeating in the same amount of time. This is useful for generating motion that loops perfectly while still appearing organic. In this particular case, the animation repeats every π × 100 seconds.

A challenge in building any generative system is to find the right balance between coherence and variety. I designed the system with the large edition size in mind. During development I generated hundreds of iterations and tweaked my code to make sure that every iteration is truly unique and fits the overall aesthetic of the collection.

I truly hope you will enjoy your own little abstract movie.

— Raphaël de Courville

15917.d:
Initial conditions are stated, and then the particles set in motion - the root of generative art. My goal with this piece was to create an illustration that seemed to be from an earlier (or perhaps later?) time; not, at any rate, our current moment. The background is a very subtle gradient; then it is heavily stippled, and followed with a particle system to create more subtle texture. (Look for the very small "hairs" in the background; they are more obvious on the dark ones. They are a subset of the main particle system.) 

Following that, the main particle system is run in real time; I like to "show my work" for generative pieces, as any collector of my previous mints knows, and this is no exception. "Run" your mint for an animated drawing experience. Note that fxpreview() hits a few frames before the end of the full run. I did it this way to ensure a consistent preview. As a result, the preview and the final image will be slightly different, only because the final image has a slightly longer lifespan. 

There are multiple "special" modes, each with a 10% likelihood: 

"spiral" will rotate the canvas as the particle system is running.
"chaos" uses random X/Y vectors during the acceleration phase, rather than X or Y.
"occasionals" adds random large particles in an opposing color.

In addition, there are three possible shapes:

"circle" draws circles for the particles.
"square" draws squares for the particles.
"jagged" draws mostly circles, with a 0.01% chance of a square at a 45 degree angle. 

Finally, there is a non-attribute feature, where the entire piece is drawn at a 45 degree angle. This has a 20% likelihood, but is only apparent on pieces that have no special, or the "occasional" special. Working the math out, you have a 16% likelihood for getting a piece at a noticeable 45 degree angle. 

All main colors have an equal likelihood, but the light background is only 20%.

These generative animations and soundtracks are constantly evolving and changing, never quite returning to their original form.

The 64 minted artworks create a series that is driven by artistic and creative decisions coded in software, while allowing for randomization.

These studies include experiments into dimensionality, shape, rotation, color, sound, iconography, layering, movement, connection, language, understanding, thinking, meditating, and communication.

Some of the visual content comes from type, characters, personal photographs, emojis, and the sounds are gathered from a variety of sources.

It's a lot to try to fit into a work or a series, but we are moving into an additional dimension of physicality, speed, storage, software, finance, and art.

The 2 dimensionality of the planes in this work is a reference to Web 2. Overlaying multiple 2 dimensional planes on top of each other, new shapes and concepts emerge, hinting at possibilities for Web 3 and beyond.

We go forward with innovation and experimentation, moving all together into the great unknown.

Gen22 is part of the fxhash live minting experience at Proof of People, London 2022.

The Gen22 system is a provocation for the future of personalized generative fashion, combining culture, history, and technology through multiple generative algorithms to produce a personalized garment complete with a weaving pattern for the tartan textile and sewing pattern for the generative garment.

The system generates a tartan textile design, a generative tunic design and a personalized sewing pattern in the needed size of the user. The weaving key of the textile pattern and the construction pattern can be used by weavers and sewists in order to produce the physical textile and garment locally.

The tunic pattern created is generated from a parametric pattern system able to create 3,125 different garment patterns in 15 sizes, to produce a specific unique textile and garment for the user.

-- Interaction --

Click ( Desktop Browsers Only )- Uses the x position of the mouse click and changes the size of the 2D garment pattern from 0 (leftmost screen) to 15 (rightmost screen)
Double-click or double tap - generates a PDF of the garment and textile patterns
Click or Tap on Textile patterns - updates the current pattern

-- Recommendations --

While we’ve worked to adapt the project to many screen sizes, Gen22 looks best on laptop and desktop monitors. The interaction and PDF generation generally works better on desktop or laptop.

Improvements in performance and processing of the voxel engine have also been worked on, which have allowed the number of buildings to be increased.

COILING 2 is an experiment in weaving color to create an orbiting sphere. Each sphere grows from a randomized initial condition. The coiling then continues to expand from 256 different rules of growth, building up each sphere ring by ring. The weaving employs a cellular automata (CA) system to generate a sphere defined by a distribution of colored cells.

Description of Features

COMPOSITION: The framing or camera view of each token is inspired by a satellite view of a planet:
Horizon 40%
Quarter 25%
Perigee 14%
Binary 20%
Apogee 1%

COLOR PALETTE: The color logic is constrained across three palettes:
Pastel 70%
Jelly Bean 25%
Neon 5%

COLORATION: How the colors are related within each palette:
Contrast 65%
Bright 25%
Medium 5%
Dark 5%

GRADIENT: The overall color gradient from pole to pole of the sphere runs through 2 or 3 colors:
Three Colors 33%
Two Colors 66%

Navigation Instructions:
1. Click, Left or Right arrow to toggle between different views.
2. Space pauses animation
3. “i” saves view as png.

15970.d:
An exercise in extending the well known and highly recognizable 1D elementary cellular automata.

The 1D CA we're familiar with involve a row of cells. Each cell has 2 states: on or off. The future state of each cell is determined a rule set, which uses the current state of the cell in question and its neighbors, typically, 3 cells in total. The number of rules in this scenario is given by 2^(2^3) => 2^8 = 256.

Hanging Gardens explores much larger rule spaces, where 5-7 neighbors are considered in determining the future state of each cell. For a scenario where 5 neighbors are considered, the number of rules becomes quite large: 2^(2^5) => 2^32 = 4294967296 rules.

Since each cell's state is determined by its neighbors, it can be colorized according to the value of that state. In a system where there are 5 neighbors considered, the number of all possible neighbor states for a given cell is 2^5 = 32. The state is used as an index to choose a color from a pre-generated palette. This palette is a deterministically generated gradient starting with a hue of relatively high saturation and brightness, fading down to a different hue of low saturation and brightness. As each row is rendered out, the index is shifted over time to create a color cycling effect.

Static rules are no fun, and even dynamically changing rules can result in static outcomes, which may run that way indefinitely. To combat this, cells and rules will mutate over time at a rate established when the piece is initialized.

Controls:

SPACE - starts and stops the animation
1 - 1-bit black and white color
2 - greyscale color
3 - full color

Un de mes frères s’est envolé hier. Ou avant-hier, je ne sais plus. Il a vendu du lest pour sortir une fille. Une bourrasque soudaine les a emportés, lui et ses deux tickets de cinéma.

Cela fait bien trois semaines que nous n’avons pas eu de livraison. Pas de courrier non plus, par la même occasion. J’en reçois rarement. Je n’ai jamais reçu qu’une lettre, en réalité. C’était une longue lettre épistolaire de mon ami Dino. Il est cowboy, dans une cité voisine. 

Mon frère connaissait cette fille depuis bien cinq ou six ans. Il étaient au collège ensemble. Il y avait encore des livraisons toutes les semaines, à cette époque. Parfois deux fois par semaine. On pouvait vendre des enclumes et acheter du petit lest. Poids pour poids, on y perdait. Mais avec ça on arrivait quand même à vivre.

C’était le temps où les rochers n’étaient pas attachés. Ils dérivaient rarement, le vent n’était pas si fort. Et ils étaient plus denses aussi. Aujourd’hui, un rocher qui n’est pas en laisse ne sera plus là demain.

À l’époque, j’étais moi-même cowboy. Je vivais avec Jacques, un bon copain. Il n’y avait rien de sexuel entre nous. On gardait les rochers. Un soir, on jouait à l’espagnolette, il m’a relancé de trois alors que j’étais atout trèfle. Vous imaginez la suite. Je ne l’ai plus jamais revu après ça.

Plus personne ne va au collège. Mon frère était d’une des dernières générations. Après ça les gens ne voyaient plus l’intérêt. Tout devient de plus en plus léger, et apprendre à lire ou écrire ne pèse rien. Plus on mine, plus on vends des enclumes, plus on peut acheter du lest. Mais comme le lest est plus cher que les enclumes, à force, la cité devient de moins en moins lourde.

Le vent est de plus en plus fort aussi. Je pense que c’est pour ça qu’il y a moins de livraisons. Il y a de moins en moins de cités qui arrivent à rester suspendues. Celle de Dino s’est envolée l’année dernière, Dino avec. Avec moins de cités à visiter par voyage, les livraisons sont moins rentables.

Avant d’être cowboy je construisais des ponts. C’est comme ça que j’ai appris à lier les rochers. Plus personne ne le fait aujourd’hui. Il faut commencer par ancrer le rocher domestique. Et après, il faut attendre. C’est la partie la plus difficile. Personne n’a appris à suffisamment attendre. Parce que plus le temps passe, plus on devient légers. Mais c’est le plus important. Il faut attendre le que rocher sauvage devienne suffisamment léger. Sinon, il emportera le rocher domestique avec lui et on aura tout perdu.

Je me demande pourquoi il a acheté ces deux tickets de cinéma. C’est toujours le même film qui passe. Je ne l’ai jamais vu. Ça parle de dialectique et de maçonnerie, il paraît. Le cinéma c’est un domaine que je trouve trop contraignant. Encore une idée de bureaucrate. Places assignées. Horaires fixes. Un processus administratif au profit de la structure sociale. Classique. Les bureaucrates commencent toujours par nous exploiter et ils finissent par nous aliéner. “Servir le peuple”, ils appellent ça. 

Cela fait des années que le pont est de moins en moins solide. De toutes les façons, on n’a rien pour le réparer. Nos rochers sont domestiqués depuis le temps, mais ils s’entrainent les uns les autres au lieu de se stabiliser. La suspension des cités, ça a l’air simple mais ça ne l’est pas vraiment. Quand elles ont été construites, avec les machines-outils des livreurs, elles étaient bien suspendues. Mais peu à peu, elles se sont dégradées. La seule richesse des cités, c’est leur gravité. Pourquoi réparer ce qui est destiné à s’envoler ?

Je comprends pourquoi mon frère a vendu du lest. Après tout, le lest est là pour être vendu tant qu’il vaut encore quelque chose. Jeudi dernier, le pont est tombé. Notre deuxième rocher majeur est toujours relié par la chaine des rochers mineurs, mais elle ne va pas tenir longtemps. La cité va s’envoler bientôt. Peut-être demain ou après-demain. Je vous laisse, je dois aller miner.

15984.d:
Subliminal is a conceptual art collection, which uses literature, and randomly generated highlights, to brings to those who mint, an original, and unique experience, related to them, and the instant moment of time, when the NFT is minted.

I decided to name this collection Subliminal because, whenever someone mints an NFT in this collection, they get the NFT they were destined to get, which in turn possibly also contains a meaningful message, that can shed more light into ones life. I say "destined" because even if the minting is randomized, if we would go back in time, and every event happened the exact same way, a person will always get the same NFT. Maybe things are not that random after all... So all that is left is to reveal what destiny has reserved for you.

It may happen that the highlights might not always make sense, or so it can seem... Though don't forget, to have a look at the page which you happen to mint too, which minimally might end up being an enjoyable reading.

For the Volume 1 of Subliminal, the book The Great Gatsby was used as foundation(a public domain published version). I have removed only some pages such as Table of Contents and other unrelated pages to the main content of the book. The list of elements of this collection is below:

Book pages: 244
Unique Highlights: 693

This collection is made with layered composition.

This is an original Op Art piece that incorporates an algorithm for drawing alternating black and white concentric squares inside a space defined by of another algorithm that divides the picture space in half (alternatively vertically or horizontally) on consecutive iterations. A coin-toss algorithm decides which half to fill with concentric squares and the other half is further divided in half again. The subdivision process iterates until the half space is too small to draw squares in.

Check out Dr. Bill Generative Art OG website @ drbillkolomyjec.com

15994.d:
Imagination Runs Wild reproduces art through painter techniques and abstract shape experiments.
It wants to show the ways an artist could follow to make abstract painting and is dedicated to making your imagination run wild.
With this project I would like to invite you to think about the simplicity of beauty and about what makes something beautiful in general.

Controls:
Press 'H' to paint with higher details (slower)
Press 'L' to paint with lower details (default)
Press 'S' to save PNG file

Key features:
8 different paper colors (some a rarer than others)
Between 12 and 30 palettes for each paper color
2 different orientation mode (square and portrait)
Monochrome (rarest)
Different painting styles...

Made with p5.js
Forever limited to 1000 unique editions living on the Tezos blockchain. France, July 2022.
